extracted.intended_audience: mathematical problem solvers (olympiad/inequality enthusiasts), researchers in elementary geometry/inequalities
extracted.subtask_description: Collections of olympiad-style problems (JP.086–JP.090) about triangle geometry and symmetric/ cyclic inequalities, each accompanied by multiple proposed solutions and lemmas. The page expects readers to produce rigorous inequality proofs using standard tools (Cauchy, AM-GM, Hölder, Jensen, Gerretsen, known triangle identities).

rubrics_metrics.name: JP.086 — inequality with incenter, circumradius and inradius
rubrics_metrics.description:
JP.086. Let (cid:2183),(cid:2184),(cid:2185) be the side lengths of a triangle (cid:2157)(cid:2158)(cid:2159) with incentre (cid:2165), circumradius (cid:2174) and inradius (cid:2200). Prove that

√(cid:2157)(cid:2165)/(cid:2183) + √(cid:2158)(cid:2165)/(cid:2184) + √(cid:2159)(cid:2165)/(cid:2185) ≤ √(cid:2779)/(cid:2779) ⋅ √(cid:2174) + (cid:2200)/(cid:2200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma provided: (cid:2165)(cid:2157) + (cid:2165)(cid:2158) + (cid:2165)(cid:2159) ≤ (cid:2779)((cid:2174) + (cid:2200)). Tools/identities explicitly cited: formulae expressing distances from incenter to vertices in terms of side lengths and semiperimeter, Gerretsen Inequality, Cauchy–Schwarz. Two solution outlines are given (Solution 1 by Kevin Soto Palacios and Solution 2 by Soumava Chakraborty) that apply Cauchy and Gerretsen and manipulate triangle identities. The page reminds the reader to use known triangle identities and inequalities and shows explicit algebraic manipulations; equality cases are indicated implicitly by standard symmetric equality (e.g., equilateral).

rubrics_metrics.name: JP.087 — acute-triangle product/sum sqrt-inequality
rubrics_metrics.description:
JP.087. Let (cid:2157)(cid:2158)(cid:2159) be an acute triangle. Prove that

(sum of three cyclic expressions each of the form √(product of three listed triangle expressions) ) ≤ (cid:2780)/(cid:2779) (cid:3496) (cid:2780)/(cid:2779). (Full formula given in the document.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various solution approaches are presented. The page emphasizes positivity in an acute triangle, writes explicit expressions of the involved quantities in terms of side lengths and semiperimeter, and applies Cauchy–Schwarz and Jensen inequalities (one solution invokes concavity of a square-root and Jensen). Multiple solution variants are shown (Solution 1 by Kevin Soto Palacios, Solution 2 by Sanong Hauerai, Solution 3 by Soumitra Mandal) that reduce the inequality to known bounds and then apply classical inequalities (Cauchy, AM≥GM, Jensen). The exposition lists intermediate algebraic equalities and uses known triangle identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: JP.088 — cyclic inequality for positive reals
rubrics_metrics.description:
JP.088. Let (cid:2183),(cid:2184),(cid:2185) be positive real numbers. Prove that a cyclic sum of rational expressions

((cid:2183)(cid:2780) + (cid:2184)(cid:2780))/(cid:2185)(cid:2779) + (cid:2183)(cid:2184) + ... ≥ (cid:2786)(cid:2183)(cid:2184)(cid:2185)/(cid:2183)(cid:2184) + (cid:2184)(cid:2185) + (cid:2185)(cid:2183).

(Full cyclic formula is given in the document.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions apply Cauchy–Schwarz, AM–GM and Hölder inequalities. The page explicitly references standard known inequalities and shows algebraic manipulations to transform sums into product-type lower bounds; equality case noted: a=b=c. Multiple solution sketches (by Kevin Soto Palacios, Sanong Hauerai, Dinh Tien Dung) show the reduction steps and where each classical inequality is applied. The solutions also discuss monotonicity and substitution techniques to simplify the cyclic expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: JP.089 — inequality for x = a/b + b/a etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solution uses algebraic rearrangements, AM–GM and Cauchy–Schwarz. The page derives identities expressing sums of these x-variables in terms of (a+b+c) and related symmetric sums, then applies AM≥GM to obtain lower bounds for each (cid:2180),(cid:2181),(cid:2182). The provided solutions include manipulations converting the target inequality into an equivalent inequality involving symmetric sums and then invoking Cauchy. Equality conditions are discussed (occurs when a=b=c). Multiple solution variants and algebraic checks are included.

The proof approach reduces the target to previously established lemmas and uses classical inequality tools; the document shows line-by-line algebraic reductions and references earlier problems/inequalities as building blocks.
